::: {#rem-halting-in-practice}
#### Undecidability in practice

[Turing machines](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine)
can simulate programs in ordinary programming languages
([the Church-Turing thesis](models-of-computation.qmd#rem-church-turing)),
so @thm-halting-undecidable says that no program can check,
for every program and input,
whether that program finishes.
A job scheduler that runs users' model-fitting code cannot predict which jobs will loop forever,
so it stops jobs with a time limit instead.
Tools that always finish and check code for infinite loops exist.
If such a tool never answered "unknown",
never missed a loop,
and never flagged a program that does [halt](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine),
then, since an ordinary language can run a Turing machine simulator,
the tool applied to a simulator running $M_w$ on $x$ would decide [HALT](#def-halting-problem).
So each tool makes one of those three errors on some program.
The proof that [Kolmogorov complexity](kolmogorov-complexity.qmd#thm-kolmogorov-uncomputable)
cannot be computed is a second example of an uncomputable function,
proved by a different argument.

:::
